questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II
List - I (Vitamins): (a) B$_1$ (b) B$_2$ (c) B$_6$ (d) B$_{12}$
List - II (Deficiency Diseases): (i) Convulsions (ii) RBC deficiency in haemoglobin (iii) Retarded growth (iv) Burning sensation of the skin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: a - ii, b - iv, c - iii, d - i
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
questions.explanation: B$_1$ (thiamine) deficiency (beri-beri) is linked to retarded growth, B$_2$ (riboflavin) deficiency to a burning sensation of the skin, B$_6$ (pyridoxine) deficiency to convulsions, and B$_{12}$ deficiency to reduced haemoglobin/RBC formation (pernicious anaemia).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: All monosaccharides are reducing sugars.
Statement II: Sucrose can reduce ammoniacal silver nitrate solution.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Every monosaccharide has a free (or potentially free) anomeric carbon, so all are reducing sugars (Statement I true); sucrose has no free anomeric carbon, so it cannot reduce Tollens' reagent (Statement II false).

questions.q: Incorrect statement about $\alpha$-amino acids of proteins among the following is
options: Methionine is an essential amino acid
Zwitterion of valine exhibits amphoteric behaviour
questions.explanation: Glycylalanylglutamine (Gly-Ala-Gln) is a tripeptide with only two peptide (amide) linkages between its three residues, so the claim of three amide linkages is incorrect; the statements about methionine, glycine and valine's zwitterion are all true.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II for the reaction pattern: Glucose $\xrightarrow{\text{Reagent}}$ Product → Structural prediction. List-I (Reagents): (a) Acetic anhydride (b) Bromine water (c) Hydroiodic acid (d) Hydrogen cyanide; List-II (Structural prediction): (i) Glucose has an aldehyde group (ii) Glucose has a straight chain of six carbon atoms (iii) Glucose has five hydroxyl groups (iv) Glucose has a carbonyl group. Choose the correct answer.
options: a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
a - iii, b - i, c - ii, d - iv
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
questions.explanation: Acetylation with acetic anhydride (forming the pentaacetate) shows glucose has five -OH groups (a-iii); bromine water oxidises only the aldehyde, showing an aldehyde group (b-i); reduction with HI gives n-hexane, showing a straight chain of six carbons (c-ii); HCN adds to the carbonyl carbon, showing a carbonyl group (d-iv).

questions.q: The correct sequence of α-amino acid, hormone, vitamin, carbohydrate respectively is
options: Aspartic acid, Insulin, Ascorbic acid, rhamnose
questions.explanation: Aspartic acid is an α-amino acid, insulin is a (protein) hormone, ascorbic acid is vitamin C, and rhamnose is a carbohydrate -- correctly matching each category.

questions.q: Which examples of carbohydrates exhibit α-link (α-glycosidic link) in their structure?
questions.explanation: Both components of starch, amylose and amylopectin, are joined by α-glycosidic linkages, unlike cellulose which has β-linkages.

questions.q: The type of linkage present between nucleotides is
questions.explanation: Nucleotides in nucleic acids are joined together by phosphodiester linkages between the 3' and 5' carbons of adjacent sugar units.

questions.q: $\alpha$-D-(+)-glucose and $\beta$-D-(+)-glucose are
questions.explanation: They differ only in configuration at C1 (the anomeric carbon), so they are called anomers.

questions.q: The female sex hormone which is responsible for the development of secondary female characteristics and participates in the control of menstrual cycle is
questions.explanation: Estradiol is the principal female sex hormone regulating secondary sexual characteristics and the menstrual cycle.

questions.q: Sucrose is dextrorotatory but after hydrolysis the mixture show laevorotation, this is because of
options: Laevorotation of glucose is more than dextrorotation of fructose.
Laevorotation of fructose is more than dextrorotation of glucose.
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives an equimolar mixture of dextrorotatory glucose (+52.5$^\circ$) and strongly laevorotatory fructose (-92$^\circ$); since fructose's laevorotation exceeds glucose's dextrorotation, the resulting invert sugar mixture is net laevorotatory.

questions.q: The correct order of match between column X and column Y is: X: I. Vitamin A, II. Vitamin D, III. Vitamin E, IV. Vitamin K. Y: i. Muscular weakness, ii. Increased blood clotting time, iii. Night-blindness, iv. Osteomalacia
options: I - iv, II - iii, III - ii, IV - i
I - ii, II - i, III - iii, IV - iv
I - iii, II - ii, III - iv, IV - i
I - iii, II - iv, III - i, IV - ii
questions.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency causes night-blindness (iii), Vitamin D deficiency causes osteomalacia (iv), Vitamin E deficiency causes muscular weakness (i), and Vitamin K deficiency causes increased blood clotting time (ii).

questions.q: Thyroxine produced in the thyroid gland is an iodinated derivative of __________.
questions.explanation: Thyroxine is an iodinated derivative of the amino acid tyrosine.

questions.q: A Nucleic acid, whether DNA or RNA gives on complete hydrolysis, two purine bases, two pyrimidine bases, a pentose sugar and phosphoric acid. Nucleotides which are intermediate products in the hydrolysis contain
options: purine or pyrimidine base and ortho-phosphoric acid
purine or pyrimidine base and pentose sugar
Purine or pyrimidine base, a pentose sugar and ortho-phosphoric acid
a purine base, pentose sugar and ortho-phosphoric acid
questions.explanation: A nucleotide = nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) + pentose sugar + phosphoric acid; a nucleoside (base + sugar only, no phosphate) is a different, simpler intermediate.

questions.q: RNA and DNA are chiral molecules, their chirality is due to the presence of
questions.explanation: The D-configured sugars (ribose in RNA, deoxyribose in DNA) are chiral and are responsible for the overall chirality of the nucleic acid chains.

questions.q: Primary structure in a nucleic acid chain contains bases as G A T G C ........ The chain which is complementary to this chain is
questions.explanation: By complementary base pairing (G pairs with C, A pairs with T), the sequence G-A-T-G-C pairs with C-T-A-C-G.

questions.q: Which one of the following vitamins is not stored in adipose tissue?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B$_6$ is water-soluble and is not stored in fatty (adipose) tissue, unlike the fat-soluble vitamins A, D and E.

questions.q: Hypothyroidism is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Hypothyroidism results from insufficient secretion of the thyroid hormone thyroxine.

questions.q: C$_1$-C$_4$ glycosidic bond is NOT found in
questions.explanation: Sucrose has a C$_1$-C$_2$ glycosidic linkage (between glucose C1 and fructose C2); starch, maltose and lactose all have C$_1$-C$_4$ linkages.

questions.q: The vitamin that helps in clotting of blood is
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of clotting factors (prothrombin) in blood.

questions.q: In nucleic acids, the nucleotides are joined together by
questions.explanation: Successive nucleotides in DNA/RNA are linked through 3'-5' phosphodiester bonds.

questions.q: Which of the following is generally water insoluble?
questions.explanation: Fibrous proteins (e.g. keratin, collagen) have extended structures held by strong intermolecular H-bonding and are water insoluble, unlike globular proteins, amylose, vitamin C or glycine.

questions.q: Which of the following bases is not present in DNA ?
questions.explanation: DNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine; uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.

questions.q: The two forms of D-Glucopyranose are called
questions.explanation: The $\alpha$ and $\beta$ forms of D-glucopyranose differ only in configuration at the anomeric carbon (C1), so they are called anomers.

questions.q: The glycosidic linkage involved in linking the glucose units in amylose part of starch is
questions.explanation: Amylose is a linear polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose units joined by C$_1$-C$_4$ $\alpha$-glycosidic linkages.

questions.q: The Glycosidic linkage present in sucrose is between
options: C-1 of α-glucose and C-2 of β-fructose
C-1 of α-glucose and C-4 of α-glucose
C-1 of β-galactose and C-4 of α-glucose
C-1 of α-glucose and C-4 of β-fructose
questions.explanation: Sucrose is formed by a glycosidic bond between C1 of α-glucose and C2 of β-fructose.

questions.q: Hormones are secreted by ductless glands of human body. Iodine containing hormone is
questions.explanation: Thyroxine, secreted by the thyroid gland, is the iodine-containing hormone among the options.

questions.q: Pick the wrong statement from the following :
options: Sources of Vitamin B$_1$ are yeast, milk, green vegetables and cereals
Deficiency of Vitamin B$_6$ (pyridoxime) results in convulsions
Consumption of citrus fruits and green leafy vegetables in food prevents scurvy
Deficiency of vitamin D causes xerophthalmia
questions.explanation: Xerophthalmia results from vitamin A deficiency, not vitamin D (whose deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia), so statement D is wrong.

questions.q: Which of the following gives positive Fehling's solution test ?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a reducing sugar with a free aldehyde group and gives a positive Fehling's test; sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct about H-bonding in DNA ?
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine (2 H-bonds) and guanine pairs with cytosine (3 H-bonds).

questions.q: Adenosine is an example of
questions.explanation: Adenosine is adenine (a purine base) linked to ribose sugar without a phosphate group, which makes it a nucleoside (a nucleotide would additionally have a phosphate group).

questions.q: Glycogen is
options: structurally very much similar to amylopectin
structurally similar to amylopectin but extensively branched
questions.explanation: Glycogen, the storage polysaccharide in animals, has a structure like amylopectin (branched chains of $\alpha$-D-glucose) but is far more extensively branched.

questions.q: One of the following is an essential amino acid.
questions.explanation: Isoleucine cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained from the diet, making it an essential amino acid, unlike tyrosine, cysteine and serine which are non-essential.

questions.q: Cheilosis and digestive disorders are due to the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Deficiency of riboflavin (vitamin B$_2$) causes cheilosis (cracking at the corners of the mouth) along with digestive disorders.

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: Lactose has glycosidic linkage between C$_4$ of glucose and C$_1$ of galactose unit.
Penta acetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine.
Aldose or ketose sugars in alkaline medium do not isomerise.
questions.explanation: Aldose and ketose sugars readily interconvert/isomerise in alkaline medium (Lobry de Bruyn–van Ekenstein transformation), so statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.q: 1.78 g of an optically active L-amino acid (A) is treated with NaNO$_2$/HCl at 0 °C. 448 cm$^3$ of nitrogen was at STP is evolved. A sample of protein has 0.25% of this amino acid by mass. The molar mass of the protein is
questions.explanation: Moles N$_2$ = 448/22400 = 0.02 mol = moles amino acid (1:1 stoichiometry in diazotization); molar mass of amino acid = 1.78/0.02 = 89 g/mol (alanine). If 0.25% of protein mass is this amino acid, minimum molar mass of protein = 89×(100/0.25) = 35,600 g/mol. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: Glucose when reduced with HI and Red Phosphorus gives
questions.explanation: Strong reduction (HI/red P) of the 6-carbon chain of glucose removes all oxygen functionalities, giving n-hexane.

questions.q: Oils are liquids at room temperature since they contain higher percentage of
questions.explanation: Oleates (esters of unsaturated oleic acid) have lower melting points due to kinks from the C=C double bond, keeping oils liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: The number of disulphide linkages present in Insulin are
questions.explanation: The insulin protein contains 3 disulphide (-S-S-) linkages holding its two peptide chains together.

questions.q: The number of moles of hydrogen that can be added to 1 mole of an oil is the highest in
questions.explanation: Linseed oil has the highest degree of unsaturation (highest iodine value) among these oils, so it can add the most hydrogen on hydrogenation.

questions.q: Sucrose is NOT a reducing sugar since
options: it contains no free aldehyde or keto group adjacent to a CHOH group
it is built up of a fructose unit
questions.explanation: In sucrose, both the anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose are involved in the glycosidic bond, leaving no free aldehyde or ketone group, so it cannot reduce Fehling's/Tollen's reagent.

questions.q: $\alpha$-maltose consists of ..................
options: one $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose unit and one $\beta$-D-glucopyranose unit with 1-2 glycosidic linkage
questions.explanation: Maltose is formed from two $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose units joined by a $1\to4$ glycosidic linkage.

questions.q: Which one of the following DOES NOT correctly match with each other?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is a peptide hormone, not an enzyme, so this pairing is incorrect; silk-polyamide, lipase-enzyme and butter-fat are all correct pairings.

questions.q: In an alkaline medium, glycine predominantly exists as/in a/an ..................
questions.explanation: In alkaline medium, the carboxyl group of glycine is deprotonated while the amino group stays unprotonated, so it exists predominantly as the anion.

questions.q: The letter 'D' in D-glucose signifies ...............
options: configuration at a particular chiral carbon
questions.explanation: The D/L label refers only to the configuration at the reference chiral carbon (the highest-numbered/penultimate carbon), compared to glyceraldehyde, not to optical rotation.

questions.q: In alkaline medium, alanine exists predominantly as/in ...............
questions.explanation: In alkaline medium the carboxylate retains its negative charge while the amino group is deprotonated (not protonated), so the amino acid exists predominantly as the anion.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Saponification of oil yields a diol
Addition of antioxidant to oil minimizes rancidity
questions.explanation: Antioxidants inhibit the autoxidation of fats/oils, preventing oxidative rancidity; saponification actually yields glycerol (a triol) plus soap, and drying oils undergo oxidative polymerization, not hydrolysis.

questions.q: The one which has least Iodine value is
questions.explanation: Ghee is highly saturated fat with the least degree of unsaturation, giving it the lowest iodine value among the options.

questions.q: A diabetic person carries a pocket of Glucose with him always, because
options: Glucose reduces the blood sugar level.
Glucose increases the blood sugar level almost instantaneously.
Glucose reduces the blood sugar level slowly.
Glucose increases the blood sugar level slowly.
questions.explanation: Glucose is a simple sugar absorbed almost immediately, quickly raising blood sugar level during a hypoglycemic episode.

questions.q: There are 20 naturally occurring amino acids. The maximum number of tripeptides that can be obtained is
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 positions in a tripeptide can be any of the 20 amino acids (repetition allowed), giving $20^3 = 8000$.
